chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does a man recite in his prayer while his garment is over his mouth? He said: 'There is no harm with that if he makes his two ears hear the murmuring (of his recitation).'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to cover the mouth while praying in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Halabi, a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the permissibility of covering the mouth during prayer provided the recitation remains audible to oneself, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the validity of the act over strict aesthetic uniformity. It highlights the practical flexibility in fiqh regarding minor physical obstructions, distinguishing between mere concealment and the actual impediment of hearing one's own recitation, which is a condition for the validity of Qira'ah in many schools.
